items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, we used to play the Sunday sessions at the Toddle House, Wardell and Sonny Criss and Hampton Hawes and Chuck Thompson and Roy Porter and all of us

ctx.x: [LAUGHS] Slim Gaillard was doing some work out at the Toddle(?) House out in Culver City, not only after that; he was out there at the Toddle(?) House and broadcasting from the kitchen, broadcasting recipes in different languages. [LAUGHS] Yeah, that was beautiful.

Yeah, we used to play the Sunday sessions at the Toddle House, Wardell and Sonny Criss and Hampton Hawes and Chuck Thompson and Roy Porter and all of us, and Kenny Bright, the trumpet, he would be on the scene with us. In fact, that's where I first met Warne Marsh. He was just coming on the scene. Him and Billy Byers, the trombone player, and fine arranger. They were just spreading their wings a little bit, you know. And Clifford Solomon, a very fine tenor saxophonist; he was just coming around by that time. And…
